_comment: Accepted pnpm-audit exceptions — task-prod-runtime-vulns (2026-08-16, round 2 per security-review PR #536). Read scripts/devops/check-pnpm-audit.mjs's module doc before editing. Every group below is keyed by exact GHSA id (not just a package name) — a NEW advisory id for an already-listed package is NOT covered and will gate CI red until it is triaged and either fixed or added here with its own reason. Every group MUST carry a `reason` of meaningful length (enforced by the guard, not just convention) — an empty or placeholder reason makes the guard treat the whole group as unaccepted regardless of severity. Round 2: vite/postcss/nanoid/@babel/core/js-yaml/qs/brace-expansion were ALL genuinely fixed (not just documented) after security-review found the earlier 'no fix below a major' reasons factually wrong for several of them — see the PR history for exactly how each was resolved (dependency bump + `pnpm dedupe`, or a root pnpm.overrides entry, none crossing a version-pins.md pin). `esbuild` was attempted the same way and reverted: forcing it via override broke `pnpm build` (Vite's OWN internal esbuild dependency conflicts with a forced newer version) — that attempt and its revert are in the PR commit history for exactly this reason, not silently dropped.

exceptions.reason: npm package `undici` is reachable ONLY through apps/web's devDependency chain vitest -> jsdom -> undici (jsdom's fetch/WebSocket polyfill for the jsdom Vitest test environment). Verified with `pnpm why undici -r`: zero paths through apps/api, zero paths through any apps/web PRODUCTION dependency — jsdom is a devDependency, never bundled by Vite for the shipped SPA (jsdom is Node-only and is not imported by any apps/web/app/** source file). Security-review (PR #536, round 2) independently confirmed this with a stronger method: a full production-dependency closure computed straight from the lockfile, not just `pnpm why`. apps/api does not depend on the undici npm package AT ALL. EVERY apps/api outbound `fetch()` call site (verified exhaustively, not a sample): finance/nbu-currency.service.ts (NBU exchange rate), finance/etherscan.service.ts (blockchain deposit/tx verification), job-sourcing/dou.provider.ts (DOU vacancy scraping), vacancies/turnstile.service.ts (Cloudflare Turnstile captcha verification), vacancies/google-indexing.service.ts (Google Indexing API), resumes/resume-ai.service.ts (Cloudflare Workers AI resume extraction), contact/resend-mailer.service.ts (Resend transactional email), and auth/auth.service.ts's TWO calls — the OAuth authorization-code-for-token exchange (`https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`) and the OIDC userinfo lookup (`https://openidconnect.googleapis.com/v1/userinfo`), the most sensitive pair in this whole list since they carry the session-issuing credential exchange — all use Node's built-in global `fetch()`, which is powered by Node 20's OWN internal bundled undici (`process.versions.undici == '6.13.0'` on the pinned Node 20 image) — a wholly separate artifact from the npm package pnpm audit is reporting on here, and OUTSIDE every one of these advisories' documented vulnerable range (all start at >=7.0.0; Node's internal copy is major version 6). Two further apps/api outbound egress paths do not go through `fetch()`/undici AT ALL, as a second independent line of defence even if the reasoning above were ever wrong: google-auth-library's own ID-token verification (auth.service.ts) resolves to `gaxios@7.1.5` -> `node-fetch@3.3.2` (confirmed via `pnpm why gaxios --filter @crm/api` / `pnpm why node-fetch --filter @crm/api` — real, separate production dependencies, not undici); and `@aws-sdk/client-s3` (documents/s3.service.ts, R2/S3 object storage) ships its own HTTP client stack, independent of both fetch() and the npm undici package. Fix path that would close this for good: bump apps/web's `jsdom` devDependency 29.1.1 -> 30.0.1 (jsdom@30 pulls undici ^8.9.0, patched) -- a MAJOR version bump of a test-only tool, deliberately deferred to a follow-up PR so this security-fix PR does not also have to revalidate every jsdom-reliant unit test in apps/web.

Transitive via drizzle-kit (tsx -> @esbuild-kit -> esbuild@0.18.20) and Vite's OWN bundled esbuild@0.27.7 (Vite uses esbuild internally for TS/JSX transform and dependency pre-bundling). drizzle-kit is a devDependency (migration CLI, invoked manually via `db:push`/`db:studio`/`db:migrate`), never an apps/api runtime dependency and absent from the `--prod deploy` pruned tree; Vite itself never ships to a served artifact either (see the version-pins.md-anchored reasoning that used to live in this file's `vite` group, now removed because vite itself is fixed). Both advisories describe esbuild's OWN dev server accepting arbitrary requests/file reads FROM that dev server — a build-machine-only surface that is never started in CI or production. UNLIKE the other build-tool findings in this file, this one was ACTUALLY ATTEMPTED and reverted, not left untried: forcing `esbuild` to the patched >=0.28.1 via a root pnpm.overrides entry breaks `pnpm build` outright — Vite 6.4.3 declares its own `esbuild: ^0.25.0` dependency and bundles/transpiles through it internally, and forcing a newer esbuild underneath it produces a hard esbuild protocol-version mismatch (`pnpm --filter @crm/landing build` failed with an esbuild IPC error) rather than a clean resolution the way `vite`/`@babel/core`/`js-yaml`/`qs` did. The override was reverted in the same PR that tried it (see commit history) — not silently dropped. A real fix here would mean waiting for Vite's own upstream esbuild dependency to move past 0.25.x (or drizzle-kit's tsx chain to move past 0.18.x), not something this repo can force via an override without breaking its own build.
